# Freight Forwarding Registry

> Freight Forwarding Registry is a structured editorial reference for freight forwarding across jurisdictions. It records the practical commercial, Customs, border, transport, documentation, permit, warehouse, delivery and cross-border context that can shape cargo movements.

Freight Forwarding Registry is designed for importers, exporters, freight forwarders, logistics buyers, supply-chain teams, Customs and trade-compliance professionals, insurers, carriers, project owners and advisers.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://freightforwardingregistry.org/): Overview of the registry, purpose, coverage, method and use of records.
- [Jurisdictions](https://freightforwardingregistry.org/jurisdictions/): Global directory of country, state, provincial, regional and international reference records.
- [Privacy Policy](https://freightforwardingregistry.org/privacy-policy/)
- [Terms of Use](https://freightforwardingregistry.org/terms-of-use/)

## How to use the registry

Jurisdictional records are editorial references, not legal, Customs, tax, transport, insurance, product-control or permit advice. Each record is intended to support shipment scoping, provider selection, route planning, internal research and jurisdictional navigation.

For an actual shipment, confirm current requirements for the exact cargo, commodity classification, Customs value, origin, importer/exporter, carrier, route, transport mode, origin, transit territory, destination, Customs procedure, product-control status, dangerous-goods status and delivery location.

## Key forwarding concepts

- Freight forwarding is a commercial service that can include carrier procurement, route design, consolidation, documentation, Customs/Broker coordination, advance cargo data, warehouse coordination, tracking, delivery and exception management.
- A forwarder can be an intermediary arranging carriage, a contractual transport provider, an NVOCC, an airline or carrier agent, a warehouse/logistics provider or an integrated logistics provider. The actual role follows the agreement, conduct, issued documents, carrier terms and applicable law.
- The importer/exporter, declarant, Customs representative, Customs Broker, carrier, warehousekeeper, transit principal, terminal operator and insurer can have distinct legal and commercial responsibilities.
- Incoterms® rules allocate specified delivery, cost and risk responsibilities between buyer and seller under a sales contract when correctly incorporated. They do not by themselves determine title transfer, payment terms, Customs legal liability, transport contract terms or insurance cover.
- International shipments can require export, transit and import processes in separate Customs territories. A carrier booking or commercial invoice does not substitute for the relevant Customs, security, transit, product-control or transport process.

## Editorial limitation

Freight Forwarding Registry is an editorial reference service. It is not a freight forwarder, carrier, Customs Broker, Customs representative, insurer, warehousekeeper, transport authority, legal adviser, tax adviser, product-certification authority or sanctions/export-control adviser. Users should verify the current requirements and contractual terms applicable to their specific shipment with qualified providers and authorities.
